blurb: Lion-maned Chinese spitz with a blue-black tongue and a stilted gait
description: The Chow Chow is a sturdy spitz-type breed from northern China with a dense smooth or rough double coat, a lion-like ruff and a unique blue-black tongue.
answer: The Chow Chow is a spitz-type breed originally from northern China and is considered a basal breed predating the modern breeds of the 19th century. It is sturdy and square in profile, with a broad skull, small erect ears and a very dense double coat that forms a ruff around the neck. Its purple or blue-black tongue and lips are unique among dog breeds.

body: Research has concluded that the Chow Chow arose from indigenous dogs in central China about 8,300 years ago. Chinese legend mentions large war dogs resembling black-tongued lions, and one ruler was said to own 5,000 Chows. The dogs were also used to pull sleds through swampy terrain, as Marco Polo noted.

The English name Chow Chow is not linked to any Chinese name and its origin is uncertain; in modern Chinese the breed is called the 'loose lion dog'. The American Kennel Club registers roughly 10,000 Chow Chows a year.

The Chow Chow is sturdily built and square, with deep-set almond-shaped eyes, small triangular ears with rounded tips and a thickly furred tail curled over the back. Very straight hind legs give it a stilted gait. The dense double coat is smooth or rough and especially thick at the neck. AKC standard colors are red, black, blue, cream and cinnamon; patchy or multicolored coats fall outside the standard. The nose should be black, though blue dogs may have a slate nose.

The Wikipedia source gives little detail on the breed's temperament. It notes that some US insurers treat Chow Chows as high-risk dogs. Character varies between individuals, and breed club descriptions are a useful reference for prospective owners.
Sources give little specific detail on exercise or grooming needs. The very dense double coat suggests regular brushing is needed, and breed clubs generally recommend regular veterinary check-ups.

A UK study found a life expectancy of 12.1 years. Conditions reported in the breed include elbow and hip dysplasia, cranial cruciate ligament deficiency, glaucoma, alopecia X, atopic dermatitis, pemphigus foliaceus, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, stomach cancer, oral melanoma, pyometra, diabetes mellitus and autoimmune disease. One North American study found the highest prevalence of elbow dysplasia of any breed.

faq.q: Why does a Chow Chow have a blue tongue?
faq.a: The purple or blue-black tongue and lips are a distinctive breed trait, and the gene appears to be dominant, so many Chow mixes keep it. The Shar Pei also has a blue-black tongue.

faq.q: How long do Chow Chows live?
faq.a: A UK study found a life expectancy of 12.1 years, slightly below the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Where does the Chow Chow come from?
faq.a: The breed originated in northern China, and research suggests it descends from indigenous dogs of central China about 8,300 years ago.

faq.q: Is the Chow Chow recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Chow Chow as breed number 205 in Group 5, and FCI countries allow a self-colored nose in cream dogs.
